result.note: Tests the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill on Lok Sabha expansion, state fertility rates behind the delimitation debate, and Andhra Pradesh's pro-natalist scheme.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill taken up in April 2026:
items: It proposed expanding the Lok Sabha from 543 to 850 seats.
It proposed reallocating Lok Sabha seats by population using 2011 Census data.
It failed to secure the two-thirds majority required for its passage.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: The Bill sought 850 seats allocated by 2011 Census population and fell 54 votes short of the required two-thirds majority. Southern states objected that population-based redistribution would penalise them for successful family planning.
questions.source: Last month, the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill proposed expanding the Lok Sabha from 543 to 850 seats and reallocating them by population using 2011 Census data.

questions.prompt: Consider the following pairs of states and their total fertility rate (TFR), as reported in May 2026:
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: Madhya Pradesh's TFR is 2.4; the figure of 2.7 belongs to Uttar Pradesh. Against a national average of 2.0 and a replacement level of 2.1, all five southern states report TFRs between 1.3 and 1.6.
questions.source: Meanwhile, Bihar (2.8), Uttar Pradesh (2.7), and Madhya Pradesh (2.4) remain well above replacement.

questions.prompt: In May 2026, which state announced the "Children Are Wealth" scheme offering families INR 30,000 for a third child and INR 40,000 for a fourth?
questions.explain: Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu announced the scheme at a rally in Srikakulam, revising an earlier proposal of INR 25,000 for a second child. Sikkim offers year-long maternity leave and IVF support instead, while Tamil Nadu's former chief minister only urged newlyweds to have more children.
questions.source: Naidu's scheme, dubbed "Children Are Wealth," will pay families INR 30,000 (USD 312) for a third child and INR 40,000 (USD 415) for a fourth.
